thread:
alice: Heads-up: Frank's integration reported a sharp tail-latency regression after they enabled function-calling + strict JSON schema validation. p95/p99 jumped from ~220ms to ~900ms. Sample request ids: r-a12b, r-a16f, r-a19c. They say it started right after toggling function_calling=enabled and strict_schema=true yesterday. Can eng-runtime/SRE triage? :eyes:

ben: Can you paste their sanitized curl + one full raw response and which model/region they used? We need traces. :mag:

alice: Here is a sanitized repro they gave: 

```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>, X-Region: us-west-2
Body: {
  "model": "open-llm-tool-1.2",
  "function_calling": "enabled",
  "strict_schema": true,
  "streaming": true,
  "prompt": "Parse invoice, call tools",
  "tools": [{"name":"price_lookup","schema":{ /* complex schema */ }}]
}
```

Raw summary from their client: `{"id":"r-a12b","status":"ok","router_ms":140,"validation_ms":460,"model_ms":185,"total_ms":985}`

carla: I pulled the traces for r-a12b/a16f/a19c. Router and validation are the hotspots. Normally validation_ms ~ 25-60ms; here it's 350-650ms. Model decode is stable. Looks like we are performing full jsonschema.validate on partial/streamed output repeatedly.

carla: quick breakdown: router does 1) pick tool 2) run structured output checks 3) run jsonschema.validate on the assembled JSON. For deep/nested schemas (lots of oneOf/anyOf and custom format checks) that ends up invoking expensive callbacks and regexes. On streaming we currently re-assemble/validate per-chunk which serializes emission.

ben: Important question — did the customer use streaming? If yes it's likely we're validating mid-stream on partial payloads. If concurrency is low but tail is high it's CPU-bound validation.

alice: They used streaming=true in the repro; they need early arrival of the function payload. Their test QPS is low (~2 qps).\

eva: ML/infra note — function-calling shouldn't increase model decode by this much; this is infra-side work. Two main hypotheses: (1) we validate every candidate emission (per-chunk) synchronously; (2) we're building full candidate objects repeatedly for beam candidates. Either will blow up tail latencies. Also custom format validators can be nasty on big strings.

carla: Confirmed: for streaming requests we run an incremental validation path that currently reconstructs a partial parse tree and calls jsonschema.validate on each new chunk. Implementation detail: we create a fresh dict from tokens and run the full validator, rather than updating an incremental parser state. That's the hotspot.

ben: Immediate mitigations we can roll now: 
- toggle strict_schema=false for that account (quickest) so router uses lenient parse path
- route this account to the fast-path router (skip heavy validation) for short-term
- enforce a per-request validation timeout (e.g., 150ms) so validation can't starve the stream

alice: Customer said they can't turn off streaming; they rely on early function payloads. They asked for us to rollback the strict_schema enforcement on our side while you patch. Can we toggle it?

carla: Yes we can toggle account-level feature flag. Effect: skip heavy jsonschema.validate path and use permissive checks. Downside: malformed outputs won't get rejected proactively, but acceptable as a remediation.

ben: Executing ops change now (internal command):
```
PATCH /admin/accounts/frank-corp/features
Body: {"strict_schema": false}
```
deploy-bot: feature flag rollout in progress -> staging then prod :rocket:

deploy-bot: staging rollout OK (router-usw2-01) :white_check_mark:

ben: rolled strict_schema=false for frank-corp progressively in prod (5% -> 100% over 8m). Also set VALIDATION_TIMEOUT_MS=150 on router in staging to test failure/fallback behavior.

alice: I told the customer we toggled the flag. They re-ran their repro and early telemetry: p95 dropped from ~840ms -> ~240ms within the first minute. They confirmed function payloads now arrive sooner. :thumbsup:

carla: Long-term engineering fixes proposed: 
- move heavyweight schema validation to an async post-process for streaming: emit tokens immediately, validate in background, and emit an event if invalid (no blocking)
- implement a true incremental validator (single parse tree updated incrementally) instead of full jsonschema.validate per chunk
- offer schema complexity caps in Console (max depth, disable custom formats)
- break down router instrumentation: measure parse_time vs validator_callbacks vs object_assembly

eva: Also add a fast hand-rolled validator for common flat schemas to avoid generic engine overhead.

ben: Follow-ups created and owners assigned:
- RT-2567: add VALIDATION_TIMEOUT_MS config + per-request validation timeout (owner: ben_sre, ETA: 72 hours)
- RUN-8812: async background validation worker + event sink (owner: carla_runtime, ETA: 3 weeks)
- MET-4590: router instrumentation: parse | callbacks | assembly metrics (owner: eva_ml, ETA: 5 business days)

alice: Customer asked for a short postmortem and timeline. I told them we'll provide a writeup once we have root cause & ETA. They said thanks and asked to be looped in on the PM. :pray:

carla: I'll open a draft PR for the incremental parser with microbenchmarks and a feature flag gate. Target PR ready in ~10 business days; canary after instrumentation.

eva: I'll add metrics to the dashboard: router.validation_ms.parse, router.validation_ms.callbacks, and set an alert if p95 > 300ms for customers with strict_schema=true.

ben: Quick logs captured during the bad run (sanitized):
```
2024-07-22T15:02:11Z r-a12b router: choose_tool (10ms) validation:start
2024-07-22T15:02:12Z r-a12b validation: parse_partial (220ms) validate_callbacks (370ms) total_validation=590ms
2024-07-22T15:02:12Z r-a12b model_decode (185ms) total_request=985ms
```

alice: I posted a customer-facing summary: "Root cause: synchronous schema validation in the router for streaming function-calls. Mitigation: toggled strict_schema=false on your account which reduced tail latency; engineering is building an async/incremental validator and instrumentation. We'll follow up with a postmortem and ETA." Customer replied: "Much better, thanks. Please cc me on the postmortem."

carla: Notes for future product options: offer `stream_fast` (emit early) + `validate_bg=true` with attachable validation events, and a `blocking_validation` option only for non-prod/testing.

ben: Marking this support thread resolved for now — mitigation applied and customer confirmed improvement. Reopening if we see new regressions. :slightly_smiling_face:

alice: Closing loop: I'll attach traces + repro to the support ticket and link the new engineering issues. Will share the postmortem draft once PR lands.
